Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

meteogal2fdata 0.2.0

Dependencies: base R + jsonlite + fda.usc

  • ‘meteospain’ and ‘sf’ are no longer used. The station inventory uses the MeteoGalicia station list service (listaEstacionsMeteo.action); the control$backend option has been removed.
  • Reading of the author’s earlier meteogalicia_YYYY.rda archives (sf objects produced by ‘meteospain’, without validation codes) has been removed from the package, together with the translation of ‘meteospain’ column names. Data should be downloaded again with meteogal2download() so that the codes are kept.
  • jsonlite and tools are now in Imports (both were used).

Validation codes, unreliable and missing values

  • meteogal_qc_codes() now exposes the official codes (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 9) with a single English description column and the default use. Package-facing variable and validation terminology is consistently in English.
  • Default quality = c(1, 5) kept. When values are set to NA a message now reports how many and with which code (and -9999). The result has attributes quality and units (units as reported by the service, unidade).
  • The daily parser also keeps municipality (concello).
  • Documentation now states what ‘meteospain’ does (drops codes 0, 3, 9 and discards the codes) and cites the official documents for codes, -9999 and station fields.

Downloads and provenance

  • Downloads remain unfiltered. New provenance manifest out_dir/_meteogal_manifest.csv (one row per file written) and attr(x, "meteogal_meta") in .rds files.
  • New format = "csv" in meteogal2download(): UTF-8 station-year CSV files with values and codes.
  • CSV files are written and read independently of the session locale (accents were lost or the file was truncated in non-UTF-8 locales).
  • Cache folders _tmp* are always skipped when reading a directory.

Functional data

  • ldata$df now has, per variable, n_<v>_valid, n_<v>_interp, n_<v>_masked, n_<v>_missing and qc_<v> (365-column matrix of daily codes); per curve, first_date, last_date and fecha (365-column matrix of record dates). The matrices (class mg_daymat) are subset together with the curves and print as one summary per curve. This replaces the nine count columns per variable of 0.1.2.
  • meteogal2fdata() keeps quality_summary (all counts), qc and fecha as attributes indexed by curve name.

Examples and vignettes

  • The Shiny application meteogal2shiny lives in a separate folder (meteogal2fdata_shiny/, same design as aemet2shiny: Leaflet station map, UDC theme), not inside the package; shiny is not a package dependency.
  • The real two-station example now uses Coruña-Torre de Hércules (10157) and Ourense (10148), giving a clearer coastal-inland comparison than the previous pair of nearby stations.
  • data-raw/build-example.R also creates a compact 2024 station summary for mapping annual mean daily temperature.
  • The spatial vignette now shows both fixed station metadata (altitude) and an observed meteorological quantity (annual mean temperature) using base R.
  • New Spanish vignette meteogalicia-es: complete workflow from station inventory and download to validation codes, spatial exploration, fdata and ldata.
  • dev/validate-meteogal2fdata.R continues to provide live-service checks; package vignettes remain reproducible without making live requests.

meteogal2fdata 0.1.2

  • Added a dedicated spatial inventory vignette and a dedicated raw CSV and validation-quality vignette; retained the functional-data vignette.
  • Added dev/build.R as a reproducible developer workflow; README.md is edited directly rather than generated from a nonexistent README.Rmd.
  • The original acquisitions vignette is superseded by the CSV/quality vignette.

Preserve MeteoGalicia validation information (2026-10-22)

  • Native daily JSON download, using base R HTTP and jsonlite for parsing. Original quality codes are retained separately for every observed variable in qc_<variable> columns. Data requests support server-side idParam filtering using the vars argument and optional native parameter codes.
  • meteogal2df(), meteogal2fdata() and meteogal2lfdata() accept quality (default c(1, 5), original and provider-interpolated). Rejected values become NA locally; downloaded .rds files retain raw values and codes. Codes 3 and 9 and sentinel -9999 are always missing.
  • ldata$df now provides variable-specific annual quality counts; fdata has a quality_summary attribute. Older archives without codes remain compatible and are counted as unknown validation provenance.
  • Resumable quality-aware caches are segregated from original meteospain caches. Incremental downloads preserve unrelated previously stored measurement columns. Added offline JSON and quality tests.
  • README and three vignettes (spatial-stations, daily-data-and-quality, functional-data) document provenance and quality selection. Referenced official MeteoGalicia URLs have no tracking parameters.

meteogal2fdata 0.1.1

Documentation, examples and validation (2026-10-22)

  • Renamed the two vignette source files to start with a letter (download-and-manage.Rmd, functional-data.Rmd), fixing the invalid inst/doc filenames reported by R CMD check.

  • Validation on R 4.6.0 (2026-10-22): 41 passing testthat expectations; successful vignette build; live API smoke test returned 7 daily records for station 10157 and correctly reused the completed download on a second run.

  • Fixed the non-ASCII source-code warning for degree-Celsius labels using a portable Unicode escape; displayed units remain unchanged.

  • Added inst/extdata/meteogal_small.csv, a six-day extract of verified historical station observations (not a complete annual series).

  • Added two R Markdown vignettes: acquisition/management and functional-data conversion. API calls are optional and never run when building the vignettes.

  • Added a reproducible data-raw/build-example.R script to create a larger real-data sample (two stations, 2023-2024) and sample inventory from the existing archived .rda files. These generated files are optional until the script is executed in R; no observations have been invented.

  • Added offline fixture tests and an explicit live-API smoke-test script.

  • Added knitr and rmarkdown under Suggests and VignetteBuilder: knitr.

meteogal2fdata 0.1.0

Initial development version (2026-10-22)

  • meteogal2inventory() reads station metadata from the MeteoGalicia service or reconstructs an inventory from local archived observations, preserving original station codes as character strings.
  • meteogal2download() retrieves daily observations in calendar-month chunks, with retries, a resumable window cache, and one .rds file per station/year. Archives are never written when a requested chunk fails.
  • meteogal2df() reads the original meteogalicia_YYYY.rda files from the older project, the new station/year .rds files, or online data. The output is a base R data.frame with standardized variable names and no spatial geometry or units classes. No missing values are imputed.
  • meteogal2fdata() converts a selected numerical measurement into an fdata object with one curve for each station-year.
  • meteogal2lfdata() constructs aligned station-year fdata curves for multiple variables and their metadata as an ldata object.
  • Functional curves have 365 observations: February 29 is removed, while subsequent days of leap years are shifted back (March 1 is always day 60). Absent measurements remain NA.
  • The package uses base R for data handling, meteospain for online access, and fda.usc for functional objects; packages for plots and data wrangling are not required.

Development limitations

  • The online requests have not yet been validated in an installed R session. The historical-data interface was checked against the archived script conventions and a station-year extract provided by the user.
